newsitem.title: UK: Bre-X not hurting Inco in Indonesia - Hand.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X not hurting Inco in Indonesia - Hand.

text.p: The multi-billion dollar Bre-X Busang gold scandal will not affect Canadian miner Inco Ltd's Indonesian operations, Inco President Scott M. Hand said.

"The Bre-X saga wil have no impact...I was in Indonesia recently and met with the government. They said Inco is a good company with a proven track record. We have nothing to worry about," Hand said in an interview.
Inco has smelting operations with PT Inco, as well as exploration activities with a company called Ingold. It has been active in Indonesia since the late 1960's.
"We have a real track record which is very important. We believe we have conducted ourselves very well which is recognised by the government of Indonesia," Hand said.
Bre-X's so-called gold discovery in Busang was touted as the gold find of the century, but independent tests showed that it contained virtually no gold.
Data was falsified on an unprecedented scale, in what has been described as the biggest mining fraud in history.
Hand said that the scandal was worrying for exploration companies operating in Indonesia, as there are concerns over the ability to raise funds to explore.
"My guess is it will affect to some degree the arrangements under the Contracts of Work (COWs) that companies sign to explore," Hand said.
Also, the Indonesian government is now floating the possibility of having any company that gets a COW to agree to provide a 10 percent free interest as part of the terms.
"That could have an impact as a free 10 percent interest obviously has to be takem into account when you judge the economic feasibility of doing a development," he said.
